demo-clinic-a.title: Demo Clinic A (fictional general-care clinic)
demo-clinic-a.prompt: Build a polished, accessible clinic website for Demo Clinic A, a fictional general-care clinic in Sample City. It offers general consultations, preventive-care visits and chronic-condition follow-up. The fictional clinician is Dr. Demo A, MBBS. Hours, phone, street address, booking endpoint, public domain and reviews are unknown: use graceful contact placeholders and navigation, without fabricating these details. Use two pages: Home and Contact. Adapt the layout of https://ravenhealth.com/ recognizably: match content width, desktop/mobile hero proportions, type scale, section spacing and surface rhythm, using original clinic copy and original assets. Do not copy source text, identities, logos or images. Include useful clinic/service copy, working navigation and an accessible mobile menu. Do not add a nonfunctional appointment form. Deliver runnable HTML/CSS/local JS. Avoid external analytics, authentication and databases.

demo-clinic-a.note: Each site is scored on its own (absolute), from screenshots, with tool names hidden. Radial Pulse generates with an Anthropic model, so scores are also reported without the Anthropic judge.

issues: Services section on desktop leaves a large empty lavender column under the sticky-less intro text, creating an unbalanced left half for most of the section's height.
Contact hero reuses nearly the same photo as the home hero, so the two pages feel repetitive and the contact page gains no new visual information.
Contact 'Where to find us' card has an odd internal hierarchy: an oversized 'Sample City' sits above a divider that hugs it too tightly, and 'Opening hours' is cramped against that rule.
'How to get in touch' card eyebrow is set larger and with different tracking than the other eyebrows, and its top padding is inconsistent with the adjacent card.
Typography is a system sans (Arial/Helvetica-like) throughout, so the type is readable but generic, not distinctive.
Mobile service card images don't span the full card width; they leave an uneven right gap inside the card.
The large empty gap between the contact cards and the 'What to ask us about' section is bigger than the other section gaps.
strengths: Clear hero with a strong headline, a short supporting line, and a primary pill CTA paired with a secondary text link.
Coherent indigo/lavender palette with dark navy surfaces gives the site a calm clinic tone and good contrast.
Section surfaces alternate (lavender, white, off-white, indigo CTA band, dark footer), echoing the source layout's rhythm.
Placeholders are honest, with no fabricated phone, hours or address, and emergency guidance is handled responsibly.
Mobile is recomposed with centered hero text, a Menu button, stacked cards and comfortable tap targets.
Photography is warm, relevant and consistently treated with rounded corners.

issues: The services section on desktop leaves a very large inactive left column while the right-side cards stack, making that area feel a little empty after the intro copy.
Imagery is polished but feels somewhat generic and repetitive, with the same consultation photo reused across both hero pages and similar clinical stock-style thumbnails throughout.
Some calls to action are secondary or indirect for a clinic visitor: there is no single dominant contact/booking pathway, and several links point to informational sections instead.
The desktop emergency/contact strip on the Contact page separates the heading and explanatory text widely, which weakens the grouping of related information.
The design is clean but relies heavily on repeated rounded cards, pale lavender panels and text-link rows, so a few middle sections feel template-like rather than highly bespoke.
strengths: The hero areas have a clear focal point, strong headline, useful introductory copy and obvious next actions.
Typography is highly readable, with confident large headings, clear labels and comfortable body text across desktop and mobile.
The palette is calm, medical-appropriate and coherent, with purple used consistently for emphasis and navigation.
Mobile layouts are deliberately recomposed with readable text, large controls, stacked cards and well-contained imagery.
The site respects the brief by using graceful placeholders for unknown address, hours and phone details rather than inventing specifics.
The Home and Contact pages share a cohesive visual system, including the same header, buttons, rounded imagery, section labels and footer treatment.

issues: On the desktop Contact page, the 'Where to find us' and 'How to get in touch' cards are placed side-by-side but have unequal heights, disrupting the horizontal balance.
In the 'Three visits you can ask about' list on the Contact page, the vertical padding within each row appears slightly unbalanced, with more space below the link than above the title.
In the mobile footer, the vertical spacing between the section headings (e.g., 'PAGES') and their corresponding links is very tight, making the groupings feel slightly cramped.
strengths: The color palette is cohesive, calming, and highly appropriate for a healthcare setting, providing excellent contrast for readability.
The typography system is well-defined, using scale and weight effectively to establish a clear visual hierarchy across all screen sizes.
The adaptation to mobile is deliberate and well-executed, ensuring that complex desktop layouts stack logically and remain easy to interact with.
The builder successfully implemented graceful placeholders for missing information (like hours and phone number) without breaking the design or sounding unprofessional.

issues: The serif display face looks like a system Times-style fallback, so headings feel default next to the more refined sans body text.
The first service card (lavender fill) differs from the other two (white) with no clear reason, and the three cards are visibly different widths in slice 2.
The clinician 'portrait' is a small stethoscope icon tile with a caption that is slightly offset and cramped under the circle; it reads as a placeholder.
There is a large empty band above the CTA and near the disclaimer (home slice 4, contact slice 3), which breaks the section rhythm.
On the contact page, six near-identical 'To be confirmed' cards dominate and the grid feels repetitive.
The footer link underlines and the bottom-border rule, which extends past the content width, look slightly unrefined.
strengths: Calm lavender/cream/sage/peach palette suits a clinic and uses the purple accent with restraint.
The hero has a clear headline, supporting copy and a primary/secondary CTA pair, plus a tasteful original illustration.
Unknown details are handled honestly with graceful placeholders and no fabricated data or fake form.
Alternating surface colours give the page a clear rhythm, consistent with the reference structure.
The mobile layout is properly reflowed, with a labelled Menu button, full-width buttons and comfortable text size.
The emergency guidance is useful and consistent across pages.

issues: Several mid-page sections use similar rounded-card patterns, so parts of the services and contact-detail areas feel slightly template-like rather than fully bespoke.
The mobile contact page becomes a long stack of large cards with repeated placeholder text, which is clear but not very efficient for scanning.
Some footer links appear as plain underlined text, which is accessible but less refined than the rest of the component styling.
The illustrations and icons are clean and relevant, but they have a simple placeholder quality rather than feeling like a fully distinctive clinic image system.
There are a few very generous vertical gaps between sections, especially around transitions into large content blocks, which slightly slows the reading rhythm.
strengths: The site has a calm, polished healthcare tone with a coherent lavender, cream and deep-purple palette.
The brief is handled carefully: unknown contact, booking, hours, address and reviews are clearly marked as unavailable rather than invented.
The desktop layouts are balanced, with a strong hero, clear calls to action, useful service copy and well-structured clinician and preparation sections.
Mobile typography and controls are readable, with large tap targets and a clear simplified header.
The two pages share a consistent visual system, including type, cards, rounded corners, colours, disclaimers and footer treatment.

issues: The mobile homepage screenshots omit the 'Preparing for a visit' and main CTA sections, creating an abrupt jump in the user journey.
The 'Full visit preparation ->' link uses a basic text arrow (hyphen and greater-than sign) rather than a polished vector icon.
Footer navigation links rely on default browser underlines that sit tight against the text, missing a final touch of typographic refinement.
strengths: The color palette and typography establish a highly professional, calming, and trustworthy tone perfectly suited for a medical practice.
The requirement for 'graceful placeholders' is executed brilliantly, using styled cards that clearly communicate missing information without looking like errors.
Custom illustrations and a rigorous spacing system create a cohesive, premium visual language across all viewports.

criteria.label: Visual hierarchy
criteria.question: Is it immediately clear what matters most on each screen and where to look next?

anchors.1: No clear focal point; everything competes.
anchors.3: Main message is findable but secondary content competes or is buried.
anchors.5: Every screen has one clear focus and an obvious reading order.

criteria.label: Typography
criteria.question: Are type choices, scale, weights, line length and line spacing deliberate and readable?

anchors.1: Default or clashing type, cramped or overly long lines.
anchors.3: Readable but generic; scale or weights inconsistent in places.
anchors.5: Distinctive, consistent type system with comfortable reading at every size.

criteria.label: Colour
criteria.question: Is the palette coherent, purposeful and readable, with an accent used with restraint?

anchors.3: Coherent but bland or accent overused.
anchors.5: Confident, coherent palette that supports meaning and contrast.

criteria.label: Layout and composition
criteria.question: Are sections composed with variety and balance, without empty or overcrowded areas?

anchors.1: Broken, cramped or mostly empty layouts.
anchors.3: Functional but repetitive or template-like sections.
anchors.5: Varied, balanced compositions that each suit their content.

criteria.label: Spacing and alignment
criteria.question: Are spacing and alignment consistent, with a clear rhythm between and within sections?

anchors.3: Mostly aligned with some inconsistent gaps.
anchors.5: Precise alignment and a consistent spacing rhythm throughout.

criteria.label: Imagery and graphics
criteria.question: Do images and graphics look high quality, fit the subject and sit well in the layout?

anchors.1: Missing, broken, distorted or irrelevant visuals.
anchors.3: Acceptable visuals that feel generic or awkwardly cropped.
anchors.5: High-quality, relevant visuals integrated with the layout.

criteria.label: Mobile adaptation
criteria.question: Is the phone layout deliberately composed rather than shrunk, with readable text and usable controls?

anchors.1: Overflow, tiny text or unusable controls on phone.
anchors.3: Works on phone but feels like a squeezed desktop.
anchors.5: Phone layout is composed for the small screen and comfortable to use.

criteria.label: Consistency
criteria.question: Do pages share one coherent visual language (components, colours, type, spacing)?

anchors.5: Fully coherent system across pages and breakpoints.

criteria.label: Polish and craft
criteria.question: Are details finished: buttons, icons, borders, states, edges, footer?

anchors.3: Clean overall with several rough details.
anchors.5: Refined details everywhere; nothing looks accidental.

criteria.label: Fit for purpose
criteria.question: Does the design suit the business in the brief and help a visitor do what they came for?

anchors.1: Wrong tone for the business; key actions hard to find.
anchors.3: Appropriate but generic; actions present but not prominent.
anchors.5: Tone clearly suits the business and the key actions are obvious.
